title: Alport syndrome: collagen, inheritance, timeline and eye signs
guide: Alport (hereditary) nephritis = COL4A5 mutation, commonest a deletion. Type IV collagen trimers and where each is seen; inheritance 80% X-linked (α5; ESRD by 30 years in males, females carriers), 15% AR and 5% AD (α3/α4; AR ESRD by 40 years, AD mild). Clinical timeline 5→30 years ending in ESRD, with SNHL (low → high frequency) and anterior lenticonus with an oil droplet sign.

title: Alport electron microscopy, transplant risk & thin GBM disease
guide: LM and IF are normal in Alport syndrome; EM shows splitting/lamellation of the lamina densa with alternating thick and thin foci (basket weave). Treatment is transplant, with a 5% post-transplant risk of Goodpasture syndrome from antibody against α3. Thin GBM disease is AD (COL4A4/A3) with microhaematuria before 5 years, good prognosis and a uniformly thin basement membrane (<200–300 nm).

title: Fabry disease: extrarenal signs and renal involvement
guide: X-linked lysosomal storage disease (defective α-galactosidase): acroparesthesia, angiokeratoma in the 2nd decade, accumulation in vessels of heart, cerebrovascular system and cornea verticillata, with renal asymptomatic microhaematuria + proteinuria as the earliest feature and ESRD by the 4th–5th decade. Urine maltese cross deposits under polarised light; biopsy shows vacuolation of podocytes.

title: Nail-patella syndrome
guide: AD disease due to LMX1B mutation: dystrophic nails, absent patella, iliac horn on X-ray, and adolescent microhaematuria + proteinuria that is benign (rarely progressing to ESRD). Electron microscopy gives the moth-eaten appearance, distinct from the Alport basket-weave and the uniformly thin basement membrane of thin GBM disease.
